public_rationale: PIMCO provides evidence for the main-driver part: unexpected AI issuance had no statistically significant Treasury-yield effect in its study. But that does not establish the separate claim that issuance had some positive effect. The Dallas Fed describes plausible channels, not their contribution to this particular sell-off. The complete causal claim remains unsettled.
limitations: A statistically insignificant estimate is not proof of no effect.
The available research examines different financing channels and periods.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Data center debt issuance has had some effect but is not the main reason ten-year Treasuries are selling off.

statement.excerpt: While it’s had some effect, it isn’t the big reason that the ten-year is selling off.

our_interpretation: The claim concerns the Treasury sell-off underway when the post appeared on October 6, 2026. Its starting date is unspecified.
The plain reading is that data-center borrowing contributed positively to rising ten-year Treasury yields, but other causes were more important.
Evidence against issuance being the principal cause does not, by itself, establish the separate assertion that issuance had some effect.
criteria.support_condition: Credible attribution evidence for the sell-off identifies a positive contribution from data-center debt issuance and shows that other drivers were more important.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible attribution evidence identifies data-center debt issuance as the principal driver, or establishes that it made no positive contribution.
